arguments.summary: Review finds two material drafting issues: NVDA’s reported first-half GAAP EPS includes unusually large equity-security gains that are not reconciled to the operating EPS bridge, and the draft overstates a comparative advantage for MU’s guidance without comparable NVDA forward guidance. A minor capacity-channel claim misattributes its evidence.

claims.text: NVIDIA reported $24.140bn of other income in the first six months ended July 26, 2026, including $23.707bn of gains from equity securities, alongside $118.010bn of GAAP net income and $4.85 diluted EPS. This means reported first-half GAAP EPS is not solely an operating-demand measure.

assumptions: The NVDA scenario grid is intended as a hypothetical total-GAAP-EPS sensitivity, not an operating-EPS forecast.
No unreviewed NVIDIA management outlook should be inferred from the absence of forward guidance in the supplied draft evidence.
arguments.counter_thesis: The stipulated scenario grids remain useful conditional arithmetic if their EPS cases are explicitly treated as total-GAAP-EPS assumptions and not justified by a simple continuation of first-half operating demand.

objections.description: The NVDA valuation bridge treats reported first-half $4.85 GAAP EPS as support for demand/mix-driven residual EPS, but the filing reports $24.140bn of first-half other income, including $23.707bn of equity-security gains. The draft does not reconcile this non-operating component before using first-half EPS to frame sustained operating profitability. The sensitivity arithmetic can remain hypothetical, but its operating plausibility basis and business-to-valuation linkage need qualification or an operating-EPS bridge.

The draft’s conclusion that MU has “stronger” current operating guidance is an unsupported ordinal comparison. The evidence establishes detailed FQ1 FY2027 MU guidance, but the reviewed NVDA claim reports historical first-half results and no comparable NVDA forward outlook. Recast as availability of a near-term MU guidance checkpoint, not superiority of MU’s outlook, unless comparable NVIDIA guidance is sourced and assessed.

The capacity claim says NVDA disclosed memory/manufacturing commitments, but its cited NVDA evidence describes land, power and shell guarantees for select AI-cloud partners; the other cited passage is Micron inventory/PPE disclosure. Neither cited excerpt substantiates the stated NVDA memory/manufacturing-commitment characterization. Narrow the claim to the disclosed AI-cloud guarantees and separate any MU capacity facts.

agent_report.work_summary: Audited the Director draft’s claim-to-evidence links, scenario assumptions, fiscal qualifications and comparative language against the supplied SEC excerpts, price panels and scenario grids.
main_conclusions: NVDA’s first-half GAAP EPS includes a large equity-security-gain component that needs reconciliation in the operating valuation narrative.
MU has an evidenced FQ1 guidance checkpoint, but the evidence does not support calling it stronger than an unassessed NVIDIA outlook.
The AI-cloud guarantee evidence does not substantiate the draft’s NVDA memory/manufacturing-commitment wording.
agent_report.short_summary: The draft preserves useful conditional scenario arithmetic, but needs clearer separation of NVDA operating performance from non-operating gains and tighter comparative wording.
limitations: No comparable NVIDIA forward guidance was supplied in the reviewed claims.
This review did not create new valuation assumptions or estimate recurring equity-security gains.
